messages.author: 839a14ba8eb0d4a0
messages.subject: Issue with blavCompare
parts:
Hi all,

Thanks everyone for the excellent R package! I'm currently working on version blavaan_0.5-2. I'm trying to run the command blavCompare using the example provided in the manual:

library(lavaan)
hsm1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit1 <- bcfa(hsm1, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
hsm2 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 + x7
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit2 <- bcfa(hsm2, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
blavCompare(fit1, fit2)

However, I'm receiving the following error:

Error in apply(diffs, 2, sum) : dim(X) must have a positive length
I tried to run the command on two distinct machines but to no avail, I'm receiving the same error. Is this a bug? Otherwise, any insights regarding how to fix this?

Thanks once again for everything!

Cheers,
Pedro

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Issue with blavCompare
parts:
Pedro

Yeah, this is abug, but easy to fix. These calculations need you to include meanstructure=T, then it runs well.

library(lavaan)
hsm1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit1 <- bcfa(hsm1, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure=T)

hsm2 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 + x7
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit2 <- bcfa(hsm2, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure=T)
blavCompare(fit1, fit2)


Ed, should we have this as a default, or how to prevent this error?

take care

messages.subject: Re: Issue with blavCompare
parts:
Hi Roy

I think with the updates in blavaan the marginal LL is not calcuates automatically anymore. Not sure if Ed plans to add it again

But for now, we could do a few edits and calculate the BF with the bridgesampling package. By telling blavaan to save some of the underlying parameters

I have doubt about making a tutorial about this, because I persoanlly dont like the BF much. But I understand people like it. Also, we could switch the blavaan recommendation from the approximate log-BF to the bridgesampling method



library(blavaan)
library(lavaan)
library(bridgesampling)

origpars <- c("Lambda_y_free", "B_free", "Theta_sd_free", "Theta_r_free",
              "Psi_sd_free", "Psi_r_mat", "Psi_r_free", "Nu_free",
              "Alpha_free", "Tau_ufree",
              "z_aug",
              "Lambda_y_free_c","B_free_c", "Theta_sd_free_c",
              "Theta_r_free_c",
              "Psi_sd_free_c", "Psi_r_mat_c", "Psi_r_free_c", "Nu_free_c",
              "Alpha_free_c")

hsm1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit1 <- bcfa(hsm1, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,

meanstructure=T,
             mcmcextra = list(monitor = origpars))

hsm2 <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 + x7
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit2 <- bcfa(hsm2, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,

meanstructure=T,
             mcmcextra = list(monitor = origpars))


blavCompare(fit1, fit2)


bs1 <- bridge_sampler(fit1@external$mcmcout)
bs2 <- bridge_sampler(fit2@external$mcmcout)

bf(bs1, bs2)

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Issue with blavCompare
parts:
Roy, Mauricio,

I did not intend to turn off marginal log-likelihood completely, and I believe the CRAN version of blavaan has a bug that makes these NA. The issue should be fixed on github, and it should make its way to CRAN in the coming weeks.

Marginal log-likelihood is turned off for some models, including 

- those where model covariance matrices are neither block diagonal nor unrestricted

- models with ordinal variables

- two-level models

In these cases, it can be tough to evaluate the prior and/or likelihood.

The marginal likelihoods that are supplied use a Laplace approximation, and I am not convinced that the approximation works well. More work could be done to evaluate these metrics as applied to SEM.

Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Issue with blavCompare
parts:
I agree that the concept and interpretation of Bayes factors is nice, and I am not as worried about sensitivity to priors as some others are. My main concerns are computational: the Bayes factor is difficult to compute in general, and there are many ways to make a mistake without realizing it. We described some SEM-specific computational difficulties in the "opaque prior distributions" paper:

https://doi.org/10.5964/meth.11167

Best,
Ed

Nevertheless, I have found Bayes factors, at least the concept of them, to be a useful entre to Bayesian methods for some who come from a (frequentist) hypothesis testing mindset.

Roy
 

On Thursday, November 9, 2023 at 10:13:35 AM UTC-7 Ed Merkle wrote:
Roy, Mauricio,

I did not intend to turn off marginal log-likelihood completely, and I believe the CRAN version of blavaan has a bug that makes these NA. The issue should be fixed on github, and it should make its way to CRAN in the coming weeks.

Marginal log-likelihood is turned off for some models, including 

- those where model covariance matrices are neither block diagonal nor unrestricted

- models with ordinal variables

- two-level models

In these cases, it can be tough to evaluate the prior and/or likelihood.

The marginal likelihoods that are supplied use a Laplace approximation, and I am not convinced that the approximation works well. More work could be done to evaluate these metrics as applied to SEM.

Ed
